standard.title: Evaluate identity and communication
standard.description: reflect on and explain how identity is shaped by language(s), culture(s), attitudes, beliefs and values, and how these affect ways of communicating
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can recognise how identity is shaped by language, culture, attitudes, beliefs and values (AC9LS8EU04). They have not yet reflected on and explained these relationships analytically — moving from recognition of examples to explanation of mechanisms, and considering how identity affects ways of communicating.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students reflect on and explain how identity is shaped by language, culture, attitudes, beliefs and values — in target language communities and in their own experience — and analyse how identity affects ways of communicating, including in multilingual and cross-cultural contexts.

nodes.label: Language as a carrier of cultural identity
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how specific features of the target language carry and reinforce cultural values, beliefs and identity — moving beyond recognition to explanation.
nodes.minimum_width: Explain at least two ways in which specific target language features (vocabulary, forms of address, cultural references) carry or reinforce cultural identity.
nodes.typical_width: Examine a range of target language features and explain how each reflects underlying cultural values, beliefs or identity; investigate how the target language co-exists with other languages in multilingual communities; discuss how language encodes connection to place, community and history.
wider: Investigate how indigenous languages in target language communities co-exist with the target language — research the history and current status of at least one co-official or community language
Research how a target language community's engagement with globalisation, migration or political change has affected language use and identity — identify specific language changes and their causes

response_modes.reason: Explaining (rather than recognising) the relationship between language and identity requires students to articulate a mechanism — 'this feature exists because this cultural value operates here'. Discussion scaffolds and case studies support the move from observation to explanation.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Investigating multilingualism in target language communities — particularly the co-existence of indigenous languages — deepens both intercultural understanding and the student's conceptual framework for thinking about language, identity and power. This is among the most significant intercultural learning opportunities in the Languages curriculum.
success_criteria: Explains at least two connections between specific target language features and cultural values or identity
Explanation identifies a mechanism — not only an example — for how language carries or reinforces identity

nodes.label: Identity and ways of communicating
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how identity — including cultural background, social role and language repertoire — shapes the ways people communicate in the target language.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify and explain at least one way in which identity (cultural background, age, gender, social role, language history) shapes communication choices in the target language.
nodes.typical_width: Examine how cultural background, social identity and multilingual repertoire affect communication choices — including register selection, topic choice, language mixing and the strategies used to manage identity across cultural contexts; analyse texts that reflect different identity positions.
wider: Interview or research a multilingual speaker about their experience of identity across languages — document insights and discuss with reference to own language learning experience
Analyse a target language text (advertisement, social media post, political speech) for how identity is constructed or projected — identify the language choices that signal identity

response_modes.reason: The relationship between identity and communication is only apparent across varied social and cultural contexts. Students who have only encountered one context (e.g. classroom formal language) will not see how identity varies. Varied encounters — including digital, community and cross-cultural contexts — build the richer picture.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Understanding how identity shapes communication is one of the most transferable insights from language learning — it applies to every communicative encounter across the student's life, not only in the target language.
success_criteria: Explains at least one way in which a specific identity factor (cultural background, social role, language history) shapes communication choices in the target language
Can analyse a specific communication choice in a text and explain it with reference to the communicator's identity

nodes.label: Reflecting on own identity as a language learner
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can reflect on and explain how learning the target language has affected their own sense of identity, perspectives and ways of communicating.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce one reflection in the target language that explains at least one way in which language learning has introduced a new perspective or affected their sense of identity.
nodes.typical_width: Reflect on the experience of operating across languages and cultures; explain how learning the target language has created new ways of thinking, new cultural empathy or new awareness of own cultural assumptions; consider the role of the target language in potential future life experiences.
wider: Produce a personal text (essay, spoken reflection, digital presentation) that traces the development of own identity and perspectives across the language learning journey
Compare own experience of language learning with that of a bilingual or multilingual person — discuss what is shared and what is unique to each experience

response_modes.reason: Personal identity reflection integrates the cultural insights from nodes 1–2 with the student's own experience as a language learner. This is the most personally meaningful dimension of EU04 — the teaching investment is in creating genuine reflective space, not scripted self-description tasks.

success_criteria: Produces a reflection that explains (not only describes) at least one way language learning has affected their perspectives or sense of identity
Reflection connects personal experience to broader insight about language, culture and identity — not only reports events
